items.note: Temples built in deficient or excessive proportion bring harm to builder and patron and are not worshipped (Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra prescription).
items.gloss: Pain comes to the builder and commissioner of ill-built temples of deficient or excessive measure, and they are not worshipped.

items.note: Spacing of larger, middle and smaller temples at intervals of nine, six, three padas.
items.gloss: Build the best, middle and smallest temples at intervals of nine, six and three padas respectively; otherwise there is a fault.

items.note: Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra's settlement terms: the city with the king is the rājadhānī, others are branch cities (śākhānagara), then karvaṭa, nigama, grāma.
items.gloss: The city where the king resides is to be understood as the capital; other cities are called branch cities; a branch city like a city is called karbata; a village is smaller than a nigama.

items.note: Defined house forms: caturśāla, triśāla, dviśāla, ekaśāla, śālā; courtyard tank (puṣkariṇī) and garbhagṛha when it is covered.
items.gloss: Roofed on four sides it is called chatuhshala; on three, trishala; on two, dvishala; on one, ekashala; a house wholly roofed is a shala; the pool in the middle of shalas is a pushkarini; one whose pushkarini is covered is called a garbhagriha.

items.note: Samarāṅgaṇasūtradhāra terms for door elements: dehalī (threshold), kapāṭa (door-leaf), door-closing.
items.gloss: The wise call dehali that which supports the door; it lies between the walls below the upper lintel; the door-leaf is the door-side, also called kapatapuṭa; closing the leaf is called varana or dvara-samvarana.

items.note: Terms for fortification: gopura (gate in the rampart), aṭṭālaka and upakāryā along the rampart, earth heap and rampart-hall (purī-saṃvaraṇa), prākāra guards.
items.gloss: A gate in the rampart or wall of the city is a gopura; high projecting attalakas and kleema (chauvara or building part) along the rampart are called upakarya (royal building); the heap of moat earth and the rampart-hall are called purisamvarana or covering of the town; guards from the rampart are upanishkala.
